text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Eight state executive councillors are being investigated by the Anti-Corruption Agency for alleged involvement in corrupt practices amounting to millions of ringgit.
-- Malaysia and Bahrain will set up a joint commission to look for ways to improve trade relations between the two countries, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad says.
-- The Cabinet wants harsher penalties including mandatory jail terms for those who cause serious environmental damage.
-- Mahathir says Malaysia will open up its financial market gradually to safeguard local banks.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says the government cannot remain interested in taking part in the rescue of NV Fokker if it is not allowed to conduct a due diligence study on the bankrupt Dutch planemaker.
-- Mahathir urges Islamic countries to work together to seek a consensus on Islamic finance and banking.
-- Malaysia calls for a compromise among members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on China's entry into the world body.
